title: Ordinals: order types, successors, and limits
summary: Ordinals distinguish well-ordered arrangements with the same size and describe successor and limit stages.
abstract: The natural numbers, the natural numbers followed by one last point, and two consecutive copies of the natural numbers all have the same countable size. Their orders are different. An ordinal records a well-ordered pattern, in which every nonempty subset has a first element. Every well-ordered set is represented by a unique ordinal. Two well-ordered sets have the same ordinal precisely when a bijection preserves their order. Successor ordinals have a last point, while nonzero limit ordinals have none. The least upper bound of any set of ordinals is their union, providing a precise limit for a sequence of increasing stages.
